title: Image build fails at test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py (v7): in-image fallback FOREIGN_HELPER not same-shaped as real helper
body:
# Bug report: image build dies in test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py step 2 (in-image fallback FOREIGN_HELPER is not same-shaped)

## Summary

Since decode-floor **v7** (`b94fdfd`, #283), `docker build` of
`ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3-instanttensor` fails at the
self-check layer:

```
#87 8.985 AssertionError: /tmp/.../overlay_after.py: refusing to rewrite the
scheduler: no authenticated identity for # [glm53-decode-floor:v7]:
v7-drop2: helper site not authenticated (sha256 386a336b... over 27780 bytes)
v7-drop4: helper site not authenticated (sha256 69e04f24... over 27988 bytes)
```

The same test **passes in a repo checkout**. Divergence is real and reproducible.

## Repro (2 commands, host repo)

```bash
python3 tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py        # PASS (adk present)
mv overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py{,.hidden}                    # simulate the image (adk not COPYed)
python3 tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py        # FAIL — identical trace to the image build
mv overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py{.hidden,}                    # restore
```

## Root cause

1. The Dockerfile ships `tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py` but **never**
   `overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py` (no COPY for it).
2. In-image, the test's `else` fallback FOREIGN_HELPER applies. That block starts
   with `\n\nclass _Glm53AdaptiveK:` (two newlines).
3. The real `patch_adaptive_k.py` SCHED_HELPER starts with `\nclass ...` (one newline).
4. The installer's `_followed_by_anchor()` accepts 0 or 1 blank line between the
   decode-floor helper and the adaptive-k head; **two** → `False`.
5. Exact-match verify refuses → `_identify()` only authenticates the
   maintainer-machine v7-drop2/drop4 recorded digests → fail-closed refusal →
   test step 2 asserts → build dies at ~42s into the RUN layer.

## Our fix (on our fork, commit 5540a76)

Make the fallback same-shaped as the real helper (single `\n`):

```diff
-        "\n\nclass _Glm53AdaptiveK:  # [glm53-adaptive-k]\n"
+        "\nclass _Glm53AdaptiveK:  # [glm53-adaptive-k]\n"
```

(plus a comment explaining the byte-shape contract). Passes in both conditions.

## Alternatives you may prefer

- COPY `patch_adaptive_k.py` into `/opt/glm53` so the test always uses the real
  helper, or
- extend `_followed_by_anchor` tolerance to ≥2 blank lines (we did not touch the
  installer's fail-closed contract — that is your surface).

## Environment

- Commit at failure: `6278ecb` (Merge #309, 2026-10-01)
- Our TP3 kit: /home/spark3/GLM53-TP3 at `6278ecb` at the time of failure
- GB10 DGX Spark fleet, Docker 28.x, overlay2
- Build log: `/home/spark3/GLM53-TP3/logs/build-sm121.log`

title: fix(tests): match adaptive-k fallback boundary in image restart self-check
body:
## Description and Motivation

Fix the in-image decode-floor restart self-check without changing the production installer or Dockerfile.

`tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py` uses the real `patch_adaptive_k.py` helper in a checkout, but a synthetic fallback in the flattened `/opt/glm53` image layout, where the Dockerfile does not copy that file. The fallback starts with two newlines; the production `SCHED_HELPER` starts with one. v7's `_followed_by_anchor()` deliberately accepts no separator or a single newline before the adaptive-k class, so the fallback causes current-v7 verification to fail. The subsequent legacy-identity attempts emit the misleading `v7-drop2` / `v7-drop4` helper-authentication errors.

This PR:
- Changes the fallback to the production one-newline boundary and documents the contract.
- Adds a CPU regression test that copies the restart test and patch into an isolated flattened directory, runs it without the real helper, then adds the real helper and runs again. This exercises both paths even from a normal checkout and is runnable directly or via pytest.

No production patch logic, image layers, launcher knobs, weights, defaults, or measured performance numbers change. The installer's fail-closed verification is not relaxed. The PR branch starts at upstream `6278ecb` and excludes our unrelated local launcher/watchdog changes.

## Related Issues

Fixes #312
Fixes #311

## Testing

On clean upstream `6278ecb`:
- Flattened layout without `patch_adaptive_k.py`: reproduced the failure in `overlay_after.py`, with the same `386a336b59e12784` / `69e04f246ae5016c` digest diagnostics as the image build.
- Adding the real helper: the original restart test passes.

With this fix:
- `python3 tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart_layouts.py`: passes both fallback and real-helper paths (including the restart test's drift/refusal cases).
- `python3 tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py`: passes in the checkout.
- Regression sensitivity: running the new layouts test against the original upstream restart-test file fails on the fallback path as expected.
- `python3 tests/test_image_layer_budget.py`: passes (`32 + 89 <= 123`).
- `git diff origin/main --check`: passes.

Before preparing this PR, the same one-newline fix in local commit `2f1e6af` allowed the previously failing image build and a real 2-node TP=2 GB10 restart to succeed. The launcher reported health passing after 125 seconds and warmup 17/17 requests successful. The additional layouts regression test was verified separately on CPU; the full image was not rebuilt again for that test-only addition, and the running server was left untouched.

`pytest` is not installed on the host, so the new test was executed directly (the same test function is exposed for pytest collection). No GPU throughput or quality comparison is claimed for this test-only fix.

- [x] My pull request has a sound title and description.

title: Fresh image build fails at decode-floor v7 self-test: Dockerfile missing COPY of patch_adaptive_k.py breaks in-image restart test
body:
## Summary

An uncached image build of `main` @ `6278ecb` fails deterministically at the self-test `RUN`
(Dockerfile step 83/90). `tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py` step 2
(`overlay_after.py`) aborts:

```
AssertionError: /tmp/tmpxgjecnks/overlay_after.py: refusing to rewrite the scheduler:
no authenticated identity for # [glm53-decode-floor:v7]:
v7-drop2: helper site not authenticated (got sha256 386a336b59e12784 over 27780 bytes) |
v7-drop4: helper site not authenticated (got sha256 69e04f246ae5016c over 27988 bytes)
```

The production patch step itself is healthy — step 63/90 logs
`patched scheduler.py (# [glm53-decode-floor:v7]) from pristine`. Only the in-image
regression test fails. **No runtime regression observed with the current `start.sh`
bind-mount path**; the build failure blocks image creation.

## Regression window

- Same Dockerfile + same test **passed at `943912c`** (image built 2026-09-28, test COPY'd
  since the v5 era, `patch_adaptive_k.py` absent from `/opt/glm53` then too).
- The test file is unchanged in `943912c..6278ecb`. The single relevant change is
  **`b94fdfd` — "scheduler: integrate #246, #221 and #180 as decode-floor v7 (#283)"**
  (2026-10-01, merged via #309). v5-era restart verification accepted the test's adaptive-k
  stub layout; v7's helper-site authentication refuses it.

## Root cause

`tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py` loads the real adaptive-k helper when it sits
beside the patcher, else falls back to a stub:

```python
ADAPTIVE_K = PATCH.parent / "patch_adaptive_k.py"   # in-image: /opt/glm53/patch_adaptive_k.py
if ADAPTIVE_K.is_file(): FOREIGN_HELPER = _load(...).SCHED_HELPER
else:                  FOREIGN_HELPER = "<stub block with the [glm53-adaptive-k] marker>"
```

The Dockerfile COPYs `patch_scheduler_decode_floor.py` and both test files into `/opt/glm53`
but never COPYs `overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py`, so **in-image the stub is always used**.
(Checked: `patch_adaptive_k.py` is not in `.dockerignore`, so this isn't an ignore-rule
side effect.) In test step 2 the stub is inserted between the v7 helper and the
`CUDAGraphStat` import; the site that v7 then authenticates (sha256 + length over the helper
span) matches no known identity and the fail-closed installer refuses — the authenticator is
working as designed; the fixture is what's wrong.

## 10-second CPU reproducer (no image build needed)

```bash
T=$(mktemp -d)
cp overlay/patch_scheduler_decode_floor.py tests/test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py "$T/"
(cd "$T" && python3 test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py)   # stub path
# → AssertionError: ... v7-drop2: helper site not authenticated (got sha256 386a336b… over 27780 bytes) …

cp overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py "$T/"
(cd "$T" && python3 test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py)   # real helper
# → scheduler decode-floor restart idempotence OK
```

Same differential in the full build: adding
`COPY overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py /opt/glm53/patch_adaptive_k.py` (after the
`test_scheduler_decode_floor_restart.py` COPY, Dockerfile:458) makes the image build pass;
container start then logs `# [glm53-decode-floor:v7] already present - verified`.

## Scope of "any fresh build hits this"

Any uncached image build that executes the in-image self-test at `6278ecb` should fail the
same way. A repo-checkout CI job (`pytest tests/` on the host) passes because the real helper
is present — the most likely reason this wasn't caught. Layer caches primed before #283 can
also mask it until any earlier layer changes.

## Suggested fixes (in preference order)

1. **COPY the real helper into the image** (one line, above). The in-image test then
   exercises the same composition production runs (start.sh bind-mounts
   `patch_adaptive_k.py` into `/opt/glm53` at container start; the mount shadows the baked
   file with identical bytes from the same checkout). Runtime-neutral today: the generated
   in-container apply block iterates an explicit `GLM53_OVERLAY_ORDER` list with per-file
   `if [ -f … ]` guards — no glob auto-apply of `/opt/glm53/patch_*.py` exists (checked), so
   baking the file changes nothing the entrypoint runs. One residual footgun to note: a bare
   `docker run` without the launcher mounts would see the baked copy.
2. **Harden the test fixture**: when `patch_adaptive_k.py` is absent, fail loudly or skip the
   `overlay_after`/`overlay_before` cases explicitly instead of silently substituting a
   materially different stub layout. Reasonable as a complement to #1, or alone as the more
   defensive option. The silent fallback is what made this invisible.
3. ~~Record the stub as an authenticated foreign identity~~ — discouraged: it couples the
   production authenticator's identity table to a test-only artifact.

## Environment

- Repo `main` @ `6278ecb` (merge of #309); regression introduced by `b94fdfd` (#283).
- 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64), Docker 29.2.1; base
  `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-arm64-cu130@sha256:905c02933be6021301db2dc284e24e3727467aa3a0f63b41d609885778a07bce`
- Build via `ABLIT=1 SKIP_PULL=1 ./start.sh start` (recipe-stamp rebuild).

title: Long-form generation (>1K tokens) corrupts mid-stream on rebuilt main image (mojibake, apologizing loops, essay restarts) — clean on pinned GHCR image + 1df71c1-era repo; k/drafter/eager/E2/MNBT all ruled out

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-impact correctness or reliability work; address next

body:
## Summary

Single-completion **long-form generation goes corrupt mid-stream** on the current `main` (image rebuilt per the recipe stamp, `eb0469f` era): literal mojibake characters, the string `乱码` ("garbled") emitted *as generated text*, English fragments (`meta-commentary`) embedded inside Chinese prose, apologizing loops (`apologizing again... apologizing again...`), the model restarting the essay mid-completion (up to 5 `# title` starts in one output), and 2–4× length overshoot. **Short generations (<~700 tokens) are always clean**; the corruption is position-dependent and appears from roughly 1K+ generated tokens onward. The model itself reacts to it in-context (translated: *"the previous two generation attempts failed (garbled), this time it must be clean"*).

Rolling back to the **pinned GHCR image (`9bb1557a…`) + the pre-E2 repo (`1df71c1` era)** makes it disappear completely (8/8 clean runs today, same prompts, same kit).

## Reproduction matrix (same 2× GB10 kit, same 4000-char Chinese essay prompt ×3 retries per cell, temp 0.7, thinking off)

| image / repo | k | DFlash2 ckpt | extra flags | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rebuilt from `main` (`eb0469f` era) | 3 | `bf582e4` (new) | default | corrupt ×3 (apologizing loops, double starts, outline degeneration) |
| rebuilt from `main` | 7 | `bf582e4` | default | corrupt ×2 (embedded `meta-commentary`, up to 3 starts) |
| rebuilt from `main` | 7 | `7d74cdd8` (old) | `ENFORCE_EAGER=1`, `EXL3_FAT_KERNEL=0`, `MNBT=1024`, no threshold | corrupt ×1, worst (5 starts, hit max_tokens) |
| **GHCR `9bb1557a` + `1df71c1`-era repo** | 7 | `7d74cdd8` | default | **clean ×2** |
| **GHCR `9bb1557a` + `1df71c1`-era repo** | 3 | `7d74cdd8` | + `--long-prefill-token-threshold 1024` | **clean ×6** |

Ruled out one at a time on the corrupt image: `DFLASH_TOKENS` (3 and 7), drafter checkpoint (old and new — both arch-identical `DFlash2DraftModel`/qwen3/5L/4096), cudagraphs (`ENFORCE_EAGER=1` still corrupt), E2 fat kernel (`EXL3_FAT_KERNEL=0` still corrupt), `MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS` (1024 and 2048), and the `long-prefill-token-threshold` knob (removed, still corrupt). The corruption also **survived a fresh double-machine reboot**, so it is not memory residue.

The one common factor across every corrupt run: the **locally rebuilt image**. Since the overlay is baked into the image build and the runtime patcher logs `already present — skipping`, none of the env knobs can disable the baked patch set.

One boot-log line that only appears on the corrupt boots (may be unrelated, flagging for triage):

```
kv_cache_coordinator.py:635] Disabling fine-grained prefix-cache hits because these KV cache managers
require block-aligned lookups: KpoolTailManager.
```

## Verbatim artifacts (from the corrupt outputs)

- `继续出错， apologizing again... apologizing again... apologizing again... apologizing about the draft, here is a degeneration attempt:`
- `（笔误残留，请删除）` — a meta-note ("typo remnant, please delete") inserted mid-prose, next to a duplicated half-garbled phrase
- `# �meta-commentary` — replacement char + English fragment inside a Chinese document heading
- `A note to the previous content: The assistant's previous response went off the rails and produced corrupted text. I need to write a clean, complete, high-quality article now.` — then a second full essay follows

Full samples (8 files, corrupt + clean), engine logs, and the exact `.env` per cell are available — happy to attach or run further experiments on request.

## Environment

- 2× DGX Spark (GB10), TP=2 over CX7 RoCEv2, `--max-model-len 450000`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.80`, `MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS=1024` (also tested 2048), fp8 KV, DFlash2 spec decode
- Target weights `Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-TR3-4bpw` @ `25a44fdb`; drafter `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` @ both `7d74cdd8` and `bf582e4`
- Corrupt side: image rebuilt from the Dockerfile on `main` (rebuild required by the recipe stamp), repo ≈ `eb0469f` (2026-09-02)
- Clean side: GHCR `ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3` @ `sha256:9bb1557a…` + repo at the `1df71c1` era

## Questions

1. Is there a known-good flag combination to run the rebuilt image (e.g. disabling the KpoolTailManager coordinator path or whatever changed in the hybrid KV coordinator between `1df71c1` and `eb0469f`)?
2. If not, would a bisect over the merged overlay patches (`#77` E2 kernel, `#86` rightsize, `#63` prefix-cache fix, spinwait, MNBT=7168 default) be useful from our side? We have a fast single-prompt reproducer (~5 min per boot + generation cycle).

title: fix(scheduler): prevent KV-blocked admissions from starving fair prefill

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-impact correctness or reliability work; address next

body:
## Description and Motivation

Root cause: a KV-blocked waiting request can win fair-prefill selection before RUNNING traversal, fail allocation only after an admitted runnable prefill was passed, and repeat that ordering indefinitely. Three new regressions fail on current main and pass with this fix.

Carry the passed runnable candidate into the next bounded turn and rotate genuinely failed selected admissions. Preserve decode priority, allocator checks, credit/debt and chunk/time limits. No launcher defaults change.

**Draft for integration:** open #80/#180 independently use the v6 marker for another helper, and #221 changes this file's ranking. This PR preserves the exact deployed overlay for review; it does not claim migration compatibility with those branches or supersede their strict migration work. Reconcile marker/migration ownership before merging.

## Measured results (separate from the bug fix)

[Report and sanitized raw evidence](https://github.com/beastllama/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/blob/dc702b4/docs/benchmarks/prefill-starvation-20260921/README.md) are included.

- On the repaired scheduler, share 0.30 → 0.50 lowered matched contended newcomer TTFT **37.616 → 23.708 seconds (−36.97%)**, across three repetitions. Incumbent whole-request decode: 21.053 → 22.584 tok/s.
- At share 0.50, four slots increased eight-request-burst median TTFT **50.018 → 65.672 seconds** versus eight. Two bursts per arm; small-sample p95 is effectively the slowest request, not a production percentile.
- All 66 measured requests accounted for; no added errors/aborts/preemptions. Five tool/JSON/code/image smoke cases passed on every arm and final production. Thermal spot checks ≤74 C, no thermal-throttling flag.
- **The 37% result measures the share change, not the scheduler fix in isolation.** No 0.50 or lane-count default change is proposed.

## Related Issues

Coordinates with #80, #180 and #221. Their helper variants are not interchangeable with this one.

## Testing

- Three allocation-starvation regressions: fail on base 775a58b704924b13cf5c38de97559b3630f67bbf, pass here.
- 33/33 CPU/source tests with authenticated deployed v5 input; 33/33 with the candidate's installed v6 input.
- Restart/adaptive-overlay ordering and Python compilation passed.
- Exact overlay booted on both TP2 ranks; image, environment, public API and final quality verified.
- Runtime receipts use recipe ca8557665bffa6529758f2c330ba8fb44c1e801a. Publication is rebased onto newer main with CPU checks; no new full Docker image build is claimed.
- Historical v1–v4 synthetic fixtures test structure, not authenticated producer provenance; inherited migration handling still needs reconciliation with #80/#180.

## Checklist

- [x] Read README; existing recipe defaults retained.

- [x] Reproducible regressions, actual TP2 boots and bounded measurements included.
- [x] No new configuration knob or default changes.

title: resolve_model_dir() leaks its own log line into MODEL_DIR when refs/main is absent (xet-downloaded cache)
body:
## Environment
- Hardware / nodes: 3x DGX Spark (GB10), start-tp3.sh @ 674155d
- Image: ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3-instanttensor
- Model: Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-TR3-4bpw, weights fetched with `hf download` (xet backend)
- Relevant settings: NFS_SHARE=0, SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 after staging

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Stage weights with `hf download` so the hub cache is xet-style (blobs + symlink snapshots) and `refs/main` ends up absent or empty.
2. Run `./start-tp3.sh` (any subcommand that resolves MODEL_DIR).

## Actual results
`ensure_refs_main()` correctly self-heals the missing ref, but it reports via `log()`, which writes to **stdout**:

```
log "wrote refs/main -> $snap (hf download left it empty)"
```

`resolve_model_dir()` is consumed as:

```bash
MODEL_DIR="$(resolve_model_dir)"
```

so the command substitution captures the log line too, and MODEL_DIR comes out as two lines — the log text followed by the path. The head container then gets a garbage model path and boot fails.

## Expected results
MODEL_DIR contains only the snapshot path.

## Suggested fix
One line: make `log()` write to stderr, matching `warn()` and `die()`:

```bash
log()  { printf '\033[1;36m[glm53-exl3-tp3]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
```

(or silence `ensure_refs_main` inside `resolve_model_dir`). Verified working locally after a `rm refs/main` repro.

Related: #52 covers the stale-`refs/main` variant (pin moved upstream). Preferring `MODEL_REVISION` when the pinned snapshot exists, plus quiet logging, would close both.

<summary>Prior PR description and historical proposal — preserved; superseded by the current scope above</summary>

## Description and Motivation

With `GLM53_MIXED_PREFILL_CHUNK=skip`, an agent processing a new prompt can receive zero prefill tokens for the entire time another agent generates. This also affects requests already admitted to the running list. A client can exhaust its idle timeout despite available sequence slots and KV memory.

Default the launcher, example configuration, and scheduler overlay to stock chunked prefill (`0`) so new prompts can use the remaining step budget during generation. Preserve explicit `skip` / `-1` and positive caps. Reapplying the overlay also upgrades the known legacy default in existing images. The launcher propagates the same setting to both TP=2 ranks.

This favors concurrent prompt progress and can reduce an individual stream's decode throughput during mixed work. The docs explain that tradeoff, migration of existing `.env` files, the existing `--long-prefill-token-threshold` option for sharing a small batch budget, and the difference between a per-request context limit and total resident KV capacity.

Add CPU regressions and a single live canary that requires a short request to answer before a long response finishes. The canary checks completed streams, the expected short answer, and overlapping content timestamps; serialized HTTP 200 responses do not pass.

## Related Issues

Related to #6. The mixed-prefill throughput tradeoff remains available as explicit decode protection; this change addresses the starvation caused by making that policy the default.

---

## Testing

Validated the exact published head, `14b6a9f6d4b6256ef4a51dade72581c4cf4a3175`:

- Eight CPU concurrency regressions pass, including installed-scheduler upgrade and idempotence checks on a temporary copy of the deployed scheduler.
- Existing scheduler-overlay and launcher-override checks pass.
- `bash -n` passes separately for `start.sh`, `stop.sh`, and `download.sh`; changed Python files compile; `git diff --check` passes.

Live runtime validation used two DGX Sparks at clean upstream commit `f906ee990596486e10ddbe381efa6f0e496f77e3`, built with the original Dockerfile into image `sha256:232573f48556c301b516ebc86a651501ed4f5c69aa72ef957168ff5a6ecd4fdf`. The runtime applies this PR's concurrent-prefill policy through explicit configuration; the published PR source is covered by the regressions above.

The recipe uses `GLM53_MIXED_PREFILL_CHUNK=0`, `LONG_PREFILL_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=512`, a 1,024-token batch budget, a 1,000,000-token per-request limit, four sequence slots, GPU memory utilization 0.87, FP8 KV, DFlash k=7 with draft TP=2, and the upstream FAT/grouped/temp-row/rightsize performance settings. The engine reports 2,070,680 total KV-cache tokens. A separate LiteLLM stream-lifetime backport is installed, and GLM-route, proxy, and Hermes stale/read timeouts are 1,800 seconds.

- Decode overlap: A completed 1,024 output tokens. B received a distinct 8,037-token prompt and answered `OK` in 9.013 seconds, with first content at 8.837 seconds. B answered 13.014 seconds before A's final content.
- Long-prefill overlap: a 999,095-input-token request returned all three exact head/middle/tail markers in 858.149 seconds, with first content at 856.319 seconds. Its short peer returned `OK` in 1.455 seconds while the large prompt was still processing.
- Native endurance: two persistent Hermes CLI processes ran from 1:00 AM to 6:17 AM PT on September 13, 2026, for 5 hours 16 minutes 57 seconds. They completed 251 and 249 independently validated file jobs, including eight and seven automatic compressions. Both lanes performed useful work for more than 5.25 hours. Their peak observed prompts were 494,550 and 494,443 tokens. Final duration, receipt, compression-continuation, terminal-error, and observation audits passed; serving and gateway container identities remained unchanged with zero restarts or OOM events. Main-agent thinking remained enabled; only compression used thinking disabled.
- Dual near-1M capacity: two distinct prompts containing 999,090 and 999,094 input tokens were submitted together. Both streams completed with every head/middle/tail marker correct. First output arrived at 1,572.371 and 1,448.644 seconds; completion took 1,572.876 and 1,452.146 seconds. Two active backend requests were observed, with zero preemptions and zero prefix-cache hits. Peak active KV usage was 87.09%; this establishes concurrent completion, not both full contexts resident at the same instant.

These are functional canaries and an operational endurance qualification of the whole deployed recipe, not a controlled throughput comparison or a guarantee of bounded latency under arbitrary load. title: feat(tp4): opt-in dense FP8, KDA large-M and thin-decode MoE on start-tp4.sh
body:
## Description and Motivation

`start.sh` (TP2) carries three performance opt-ins: FP8 weight-only dense projections (`GLM53_DENSE_FP8`), KDA BF16 large-M prefill (`GLM53_KDA_BF16_LARGE_M`) and the SM121 thin-decode routed-expert kernels (`GLM53_EXL3_MOE_FAST`). `start-tp4.sh` did not wire any of them (`GLM53_DENSE_FP8 is not wired here`), so a four-node kit could not use them.

This PR wires them on the four-node launcher the same way the other TP4 opt-ins are wired (adaptive-k in #235, the slice in #224):

- **Opt-in only, TP4-scoped.** All three are reset to `off`/`0`/`0` before `.env.tp4` is sourced, so a shared TP2 `.env` (whose template sets `GLM53_DENSE_FP8=all`) cannot switch them on for four nodes; caller exports beat `.env.tp4`, and the source is logged once. This is the same capture/reset pattern as `GLM53_ADAPTIVE_K`.
- **Fail closed.** `GLM53_DENSE_FP8` accepts only canonical values (`off`, `all`, or a `shared,dense,kda,mla` list); `GLM53_KDA_BF16_LARGE_M=1` requires the `kda` group; booleans use the existing `_glm53_validate_enum`. With `GLM53_EXL3_MOE_FAST=1`, the launcher probes `exllamav3_ext.glm53_fast_moe_version() == 1` on every rank before `restart` stops anything, then again after image preparation, so a stock image is refused rather than silently served.
- **Off mode unchanged.** With all three off nothing new is staged, mounted or installed; rank scripts run `patch_dense_fp8.py` only when it is mounted (the `start-tp3.sh` pattern).
- **KDA shape.** The overlay's exact-shape allowlist gains the TP4-local `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` shape `[6416,4096]` (16 local heads × 385 rows + 256 replicated `f_a`/`g_a` rows), retaining 50.1 MiB/layer-rank, ~1.66 GiB/rank. SM121/dtype checks and the fixed `M>512` boundary are unchanged. Because `overlay/exl3.py` changed (only that dict entry and strings), the cooperative-MoE profile generators are repinned, following the two previous repins in the CHANGELOG.

One operational finding is documented: after building the decode-pipeline image with `BUILD=1`, a later `SKIP_BUILD=1` restart re-pulls GHCR over the local build (by design of `ensure_image`). The FAST preflight caught it on hardware and refused before stopping the serve; the refusal and docs now say to restart with `SKIP_PULL=1`.

## Related Issues

- #235 and #224 (same TP4 wiring pattern)
- `docs/adopt-fp8-all-kda-bf16-2026-09-26.md` (TP2 adoption evidence and numerics method this follows)

---

## Testing

CPU, on this branch:

```
$ python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_tp4_perf_wiring.py tests/test_kda_bf16_large_m.py \
    tests/test_tp4_adaptive_k_wiring.py tests/test_exl3_decode_pipeline.py tests/test_sparse_mla_slice.py
52 passed, 19 skipped
$ bash tests/test_default_reasoning_effort_tp4.sh && bash -n start-tp4.sh && echo OK
OK
```

`tests/test_tp4_perf_wiring.py` (new): `test_tp4_does_not_inherit_shared_performance`, `test_caller_setness`, `test_invalid_before_actions_and_kda_dependency`, `test_management_and_off_skip_probes`, `test_performance_sources_and_acceptance`, `test_missing_image_skips_only_pre_stop_probe`, `test_missing_artifacts_and_worker_probe_fail_before_stop`, `test_wiring_mounts_delivery_order_and_off_trace`, `test_tp4_shape_contract`. They fail on `674155d` and pass here. The 19 skips are the CPU-PyTorch tensor tests; with torch installed, `tests/test_kda_bf16_large_m.py` gives 27 passed.

**Boot on a 4× DGX Spark kit.** Image rebuilt from this branch (`BUILD=1 GLM53_EXL3_MOE_FAST=0 ./start-tp4.sh restart`, which includes `overlay/patch_exl3_decode_pipeline.py`) and shipped to ranks 1–3. Both arms use that image and branch, and are launched with `SKIP_BUILD=1 SKIP_PULL=1 ./start-tp4.sh restart`. The config is `.env.tp4.example` defaults plus `GLM53_ADAPTIVE_K=ema` (k-set 2,4,7), `DFLASH_TOKENS=7`, `MAX_NUM_SEQS=8`, MNBT 2048, 1M ctx. The arms differ only in caller exports. The A/B below ran on an earlier revision of this branch. It had the same `overlay/exl3.py` bytes, image, mounts and installer order; only the launcher's knob parsing and logging were simplified afterwards. The final commit was then booted on the same kit with the knobs only in `.env.tp4`. Every rank (0–3) logs the first two lines, the launcher logs the third, and the FAST extension probe passes on all four ranks before the stop:

```
dense fp8 groups: all; dense exl3: 0
kda bf16-large-m retained for kda [6416x4096] +50.1 MiB/rank (M>512), dtype=bfloat16     (x34)
[glm53-exl3-tp4] tp4 perf: dense_fp8=all (.env.tp4) kda_bf16=1 (.env.tp4) fast=1 (.env.tp4)
GPU KV cache size: 4,212,338 tokens        (A/B: on 4,213,773, off 4,248,206)
```

`tests/bench_decode.py`: 5 runs × 400 tokens per workload, temperature 0, thinking off, quiet serve (0 intervals with ≥2 requests in flight during either bench). Cold prefill uses fresh 11k/55k/191k prompts.

| | all off | FP8 `all` + KDA large-M + FAST | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Structured decode tok/s (median) | 97.9 | **120.1** | +22.7 % |
| Prose decode tok/s | 42.9 | **54.0** | +25.9 % |
| Coding decode tok/s | 61.9 | **79.3** | +28.1 % |
| Accepted tokens / step (prose) | 2.02 | 2.11 | |
| Coding TTFT | 0.28 s | 0.22 s | |
| Cold prefill 11k / 55k / 191k tok/s | 1,471 / 1,515 / 1,467 | 1,517 / 1,434 / 1,474 | +3 / −5 / +0.5 % |
| Cached 55k repeat | 0.88 s | 0.81 s | |
| GPU KV tokens | 4,248,206 | 4,213,773 | −0.8 % |
| Boot to ready (incl. post-ready warmup + canary) | 498 s | 801 s | +303 s |
| Head / min-node MemAvailable after bench | 6.5 / 6.5 GiB | 6.3 / 6.3 GiB | |

**Numerics.** Prompt NLL from `prompt_logprobs`, prefill-only, on ~11.7k tokens of code and ~11.1k tokens of prose, with three stock (all-off) boots as the control:

| nats/token | stock range (3 boots) | on |
|---|---:|---:|
| code | 1.0053 – 1.0087 | 1.0046 |
| prose | 1.9871 – 1.9890 | 1.9908 |

Both stay within `max(stock range, 0.005)`, the tolerance used in the TP2 numerics study. `tests/eval_coop_quality.py` (greedy probes) passed on both arms. The only NVRM lines (`NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY`, head only) fall in the first second of the logprob probe in *both* arms, and are 0 outside it.

Caveats stated for the record:
- One boot per arm, not A/B/A, and no per-feature attribution. The decode gain is the combined effect.
- KDA large-M's TP2 prefill gain (−11–14 % TTFT) does **not** reproduce at TP4. Prefill is flat within noise, and 55k is 5 % slower in this single pair. It still costs ~1.66 GiB/rank; a TP4 kit may prefer `GLM53_DENSE_FP8=all GLM53_EXL3_MOE_FAST=1` alone.
- Boot is ~5 minutes longer with all three on.
- The config is now the live serve on this kit. A plain `SKIP_BUILD=1 ./start-tp4.sh restart` with the knobs only in `.env.tp4` (plus `SKIP_PULL=1`) came back with the same log lines on all four ranks and passed the post-ready canary.

## Description and Motivation

`start.sh` has carried adaptive verification length (`GLM53_ADAPTIVE_K=ema` and its six companion knobs, *Faster prose decode*, 2026-09-08) with a capture-size generator that adds every enabled query length at every batch size. `start-tp4.sh` never forwarded the knobs, mounted `overlay/patch_adaptive_k.py`, or extended the capture list, so a four-node kit that set `GLM53_ADAPTIVE_K=ema` got stock k on every rank with no error and no log line.

This PR wires the overlay on the four-node launcher exactly the way the other TP4 overlays are wired (and the way #224 did for the slice): host path, existence check, scp to ranks 1–3, read-only mount, container-start application on head and workers, env forwarded to head and workers, and the identical capture-size generator from `start.sh` (identity when `off`). No new knob, no new default; `GLM53_ADAPTIVE_K` stays `off`. `GLM53_DENSE_FP8` is deliberately not wired (numerics still marked provisional in the README).

**Measured effect on a 4× DGX Spark kit** (see Testing): with `ema` the drafter still proposes 7, the scheduler verifies 3/5/8-token prefixes, and prose acceptance ratio goes 0.34 → 0.50 with fewer wasted verify positions. Single-stream decode moved structured 86.9 → 100.5, coding 57.5 → 63.8, prose 41.0 → 42.7 tok/s across a boot that also switched mixed prefill `skip` → `fair` and set `GLM53_APC_RETENTION_INTERVAL_SWA=0` (both already the `.env.tp4.example` defaults), so the decode delta is not attributed to adaptive-k alone. The claim of this PR is that the knob now reaches every rank on TP=4; the speed claim is the README's TP2 one.

## Related Issues

- #224 (same launcher wiring pattern; measurement boot ran both)
- Closes nothing; no issue was filed because the knob silently did nothing on TP=4 rather than failing.

title: fix(coop): validate source provenance instead of ELF hash

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-impact correctness or reliability work; address next

body:
## Summary

The TP2 cooperative MoE profile currently requires one pre-recorded `cooperative_moe.so` SHA-256. Clean source builds can legitimately produce a different ELF when CUDA, the host compiler, system headers, build IDs, or fatbin metadata differ, leaving users unable to select an otherwise valid source-built extension.

This replaces that repository-wide output hash with reviewed source provenance and native compatibility checks.

## What changed

- `build.sh` now emits `build-manifest.json` with:
  - the pinned ExLlamaV3 commit and combined input-tree digest
  - hashes of the native sources, runtime adapter, and build recipe
  - the reviewed SM121a target and compile flags
  - CUDA, host compiler, and system provenance
  - a per-build output digest for artifact/transfer integrity
- avoidable compiler variance is reduced with a fixed locale, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, and CUDA `--frandom-seed`
- `prepare_profile.py` validates the manifest, AArch64 ELF shape, and required `glm53_coop_*` symbols instead of comparing against one globally allowed ELF hash
- runtime still fails closed on the native ABI, exact layout, and occupancy checks
- documentation and profile-integrity tests cover the new workflow

The per-build output digest only binds a manifest to its artifact. It is not a pre-recorded allowlist, so a different valid toolchain build can carry its own digest.

## Validation

- two isolated builds from the same pinned image and inputs were byte-identical
- both generated manifests passed profile preparation
- 10 profile-integrity tests passed, including source/recipe drift, wrong architecture/symbols, artifact substitution, and acceptance of different valid compiler output
- 57 CPU dispatch checks passed
- optimized (`python -O`) native initialization regression passed
- 48-check numerical/CUDA-graph integration gate passed on both DGX Spark GPUs
- bounded `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` gate passed on both GPUs with zero errors
- a two-node opt-in serve prepared all 42 cooperative layers on both ranks

Performance qualification also showed the intended shape: the kernel was strongest for low-row and expert-reuse cases, while the existing FAST path remained the better default for the current DFlash2 agentic replay. Cooperative mode therefore remains explicit opt-in.

```bash
bash -n extensions/cooperative_moe/build.sh
python3 extensions/cooperative_moe/test_profile.py
python3 extensions/cooperative_moe/test_dispatch.py
python3 -O extensions/cooperative_moe/test_optimized_init.py
```

title: fix(scheduler): honor request priority in fair prefill

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-impact correctness or reliability work; address next

body:
## Description and Motivation

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, the fair-prefill candidate ranking in `overlay/patch_scheduler_decode_floor.py` (`_rank_prefills`) sorted only by service age, round-robin and arrival time — a queued lower-priority request was admitted before a higher-priority one.

Live reproduction on a 2-node kit (recipe `6961fa0`, v5 helper): with four slots occupied, a family request (priority 0) queued before an owner request (priority −10) that was submitted later. Pre-fix the owner waited behind the older family request in two observed runs; post-fix the owner is admitted first. Queue-order receipts (request ids, priorities, timestamps) retained.

The fix adds a priority key to the ranking **only** when the scheduler policy is `priority`; under the default FCFS policy the key is a constant `0` and the ranking is byte-for-byte the previous one. Within a priority tier, the existing service-age/round-robin fairness is preserved. Service-time credit, chunk limits and running-decoder protection are unchanged.

Installed v5 helpers are migrated in place via two exact anchors (fail-closed: a drifted or missing anchor aborts before any write — there is a single `write_text` at the end of the branch, so no partial writes). Repeated application is byte-identical, and a migrating run logs `migrated prefill-priority ranking` distinctly from the no-op `already present — verified`.

- Coordinates with open draft #180 (same installer file; its inspected head `4ffef088` does not contain this fix) and with #80's canonical-helper migration registry. This PR adds the marker `[glm53-prefill-priority:v1]` and deliberately does not reuse #180's reserved version identifiers. ## What this adds

Five field-notes documents from a **second 2×Spark kit** (`spark-d931` / `spark-ea54`, 2×GB10
SM121a, TP2 over CX7), recipe checkout `943912c`, image built from this repo's Dockerfile. All
measurements are same-machine A/B with the engine warm and idle; each arm's `.env` snapshot and
the bench JSON are kept on the reporting kit.

1. `docs/cooperative-moe-worker-gate-20260928.md`
   **Closes two open items** in `docs/cooperative-moe.md` → *Remaining work*: the
   **worker-node GPU gate** (now 48/48 pass, exit 0) and **geometry-1 capture-size coverage**
   (`capture_rows` includes 3 and 5, the live adaptive-k sizes). Also records the digest-repin
   problem: the pinned `aa3fe5e9…` never existed on this kit, a clean rebuild produces a
   different digest and is not even deterministic across runs (two builds: `f3a228da…`,
   `a8c75190…`), and the quickstart's "stop" rule conflicts with the handoff's "gate, then
   repin" rule. The doc gives the order that satisfies both (rebuild → repin → generate overlay

2. `docs/cx7-dual-rail-gid-notes.md`
   A real failure mode: NetworkManager's default `ipv6.addr-gen-mode=stable-privacy` adds a
   second IPv6 link-local, which pushes the IPv4 GID from index 2/3 to 5/6 on that HCA. On a
   dual-rail kit there is then **no single GID index valid on both listed devices**, so the
   preflight refuses to start (`worker GID index 3 is EMPTY on rocep1s0f0`). Includes the
   deterministic fix (`ipv6.addr-gen-mode eui64` + an mlx5 device rebind, since a flush/re-add
   is not enough), the GID tables before/after, a companion note about an error-ignoring
   one-shot unit whose rail-2 address silently disappears, and a same-machine dual-rail A/B
   (raw rails 108.94 / 108.91 Gb/s; cold 21.2k prefill **14.13 s vs 14.84 s, +5.0 %**;
   decode neutral at ×1 and ×8).

3. `docs/moe-fast-x-coop-composition.md`
   Fills the "Composition with the cooperative-MoE path is untested" line in
   `docs/sm121-perf-paths.md`: with the coop overlay active, `MOE_FAST=0` drops structured ×1
   from **80.20 → 44.88 tok/s (−44 %)** and ×8 aggregate by 11 %. The composition is
   load-bearing — coop's 1–32-row window leaves a lot of decode work (and, at ≥6 concurrent
   sequences, most rows) on the fused path that `MOE_FAST` accelerates.

4. `docs/air-gapped-build.md`
   The offline build recipe for hosts with no route to docker.io / pypi.org / codeload (both
   machines here are in that state): vendor the ExLlamaV3 tarball and the `instanttensor` wheel
   from a machine that does have internet, the five Dockerfile edits, and the BuildKit pitfall
   worth knowing — **a digest-pinned `FROM` sends a manifest HEAD to the registry even when the
   image is already local**, which is the confusing error most likely to be hit.

5. `docs/tuning-findings-20260928.md`
   Serving data on this kit: concurrency sweep ×1…×8 (prose ×8 aggregate **124.5 tok/s**,
   structured ×1 83.5), the `MAX_NUM_SEQS` / `EXL3_TEMP_ROWS_FUSED` interaction, dense-FP8 group
   A/B (`dense,kda` → `shared,dense,kda,mla`: +4.5 % ×1, +15.5 % ×8, with the PROVISIONAL
   numerics caveat and a note that the in-repo coherence check is a smoke test, not a gate),
   adaptive-k on/off, a null result on cudagraph-list density (15 vs 20 entries), the cost of a
   boot-time `-lgc 0,2200` cap (~6 % and a per-rank mismatch becomes the cluster ceiling), and
   cgroup-level memory accounting for why the head runs ~1.8 GB tighter than the headless worker
   on UMA.

## Suggested follow-ups for maintainers

* `docs/cooperative-moe-quickstart.md`: replace the bare "if a clean rebuild differs … stop"
  with the explicit repin order (and say that a differing digest is expected when the pin was
  built on another kit).

title: Display-reserve KV: +1.75 GiB of KV cache per Spark from the GB10 framebuffer carveout

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Important scoped work; schedule after P0 and P1

body:
## Summary

GB10 firmware reserves ~2 GiB of unified memory for display scanout that CUDA never sees. On a headless Spark this is wasted. This PR reclaims 1.75 GiB per rank as **additional** KV-cache backing.

**Credit:** the idea and the reference implementation come from [coolbho3k/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-2x-DGX-Spark](https://github.com/coolbho3k/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-2x-DGX-Spark) (`release/runtime/sources/display_kv.c`, AGPL-3.0, "2GB free RAM unlock" in the [author's NVIDIA forum post](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/deepseek-v4-1-flash-for-2x-dgx-spark-exl3-3bpw-3m-kv-cache-c6-new-2gb-free-ram-unlock/383583)). `overlay/display_kv/display_kv.c` is a port of that file, simplified to a display-only span with configurable DRM node/size; the vLLM wiring is new and specific to this recipe's allocation paths.

## How it works

1. With `nvidia_drm modeset=1 fbdev=0` and no desktop, `/dev/dri/card0` accepts `DRM_IOCTL_MODE_CREATE_DUMB`. A 4096-px × 32-bpp dumb buffer of `GLM53_DISPLAY_KV_MIB` is allocated **from the display reservation** (`MemAvailable` moves by 0 when it is touched).
2. `MAP_DUMB` + `mmap(MAP_SHARED)` + `cuMemHostRegister(DEVICEMAP|IOMEMORY)`. On the unified GB10 the device pointer equals the host pointer; the library asserts this.
3. `gpu_worker.determine_available_memory` opens the pool once per rank and **adds** it to `available_kv_cache_memory_bytes`. Ordinary budget (`GPU_MEM_UTIL`, profile run, graph reserve) is untouched.
4. The KV tensor allocators (`gpu_model_runner._allocate_kv_cache_tensors`, v2 `gpu/attn_utils._allocate_kv_cache`, and the cross-layer mixin) plan first-fit-decreasing over the tensor list and carve the largest tensors that fit from the pool as zero-copy `torch.as_tensor` views; the rest use `torch.zeros` as before. 11 MiB stranded on this kit.

## Launcher

| knob | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `GLM53_DISPLAY_KV` | `auto` | `1` = required (boot fails without the pool), `auto` = use when both hosts report `modeset=Y fbdev=N` and the DRM node exists, `0` = never touch DRM |
| `GLM53_DISPLAY_KV_MIB` | `1792` | multiple of 16; 2032 is the largest that allocates (2048 → ENOMEM) |
| `HEAD_DRM_CARD` / `WORKER_DRM_CARD` | `/dev/dri/card0` | mapped to `/dev/dri/card0` in each container |

Preflight checks the module parameters on both hosts (via `sudo -n` where the sysfs files are root-only), builds `libglm53_display_kv.so` inside the serving image if stale (so the `.so` is not committed), stages it to the worker, and adds only `--device <card>:/dev/dri/card0`. No privileged container, no host changes by the launcher. `patch_display_kv.py` is idempotent and fails closed on anchor drift like the other overlays.

**Host prerequisite** (one time, documented in `docs/display-kv.md`): DGX OS ships `/etc/modprobe.d/zz-nvidia-drm-override.conf` with `modeset=0`; it must become `options nvidia_drm modeset=1 fbdev=0` + `update-initramfs`, or a guarded `rmmod/modprobe` while idle. `auto` degrades gracefully when this has not been done.

## Measured (this 2× kit, driver 580.173.02, 262k ctx, util 0.87, c8, NVMe offload on)

- Head KV budget **13.7 → 16.52 GiB**, block pool **530 → 610** (+80 blocks); worker 15.45 GiB.
- Pool bandwidth (standalone probe, `overlay/display_kv/probe_main.cu`): read **162 GB/s**, write 114 GB/s — identical to ordinary `cuMemHostRegister`'d host memory, vs 235/196 GB/s for `cudaMalloc`. Blocks that land in the pool are read at ~69 % of normal.
- Cold 133,311-token needle-in-haystack: correct answer, 1,315 tok/s prefill. Warm repeat: cached hit, correct.
- c4 decode 300 tok each: 16.7–17.7 tok/s per stream, 66.8 aggregate (unchanged vs before on this config).
- Boot log per rank:
  ```
  [glm53-display-kv] {"stage": "pool_open", "bytes": 1879048192, "mib": 1792, ...}
  [glm53-display-kv] {"stage": "plan", "tensors": 22, "from_pool": 7, "planned_mib": 1780, "stranded_mib": 11}
  [glm53-display-kv] {"stage": "kv_allocated", ..., "tensors_ordinary": 15, "unused_pool_mib": 11}
  ```

## Caveats

- It does not create memory; the remaining ~256 MiB of the reservation is not extra headroom, and host-RAM preflight is unchanged.
- Lower bandwidth for the blocks that live there (see above).
- Any display workload (monitor, remote desktop, `display-manager`) competes for the region — keep both Sparks headless.
- Qualified on 580.173.02 only.

## Tests

- `tests/test_display_kv_patch.py` (CPU): idempotent apply, fail-closed on duplicate/partial anchors, v1+v2 anchors reference the plan and index, knob parsing rejects typos, FFD plan, `0` mode never touches DRM. 5 passed.
- Live: two full boots on the kit (first exposed that this image takes the v2 runner path — `gpu/attn_utils._allocate_kv_cache` — now covered).

title: perf(sm121): add opt-in SENS8 decode routing for TP2

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low urgency, experimental, stale, or needs more evidence

body:
## What

Opt-in request-local SENS8 restricts each speculative verify block to a 28-expert coreset (from 288), reducing routed-expert weight traffic on TP2/SM121. Dynamic device metadata keeps request boundaries graph-safe without partition-specific graph keys.

## Why

Decode MoE is expert-weight-bandwidth bound, not GEMV bound: typical M=8 verify touches ~38 unique experts/layer; the coreset cuts that to ~27 (-28%), saving ~21% routed-MoE time per layer for ~+30us/layer router cost.

## Scope

- TP2, 2x GB10 / SM121, opt-in, speculative verify only, C=28 fixed (internal constant, not a knob), prefill/no-spec fallback stock. TP3 unsupported (fail-closed).
- `GLM53_SENS8_ROUTER=0|1`, default 0. Flag off leaves the stock router path literally untouched (integration not installed; proven zero sens8 log lines + wrapper-identity unit test).

title: worker docker load fails "max depth exceeded" on main@b356b2c: recipe is back over overlay2's practical ~125-layer budget (126 layers)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Immediate safety: host loss, silent corruption, or sustained outage

body:
## Environment

- Hardware / nodes: 2x DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified), TP=2 via `./start.sh` (head `spark-d3c7`, worker `vp309@192.168.4.2`)
- Interconnect: LAN + ssh (the image is shipped head→worker with `docker save | ssh docker load`)
- Image: `ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3-instanttensor`, locally rebuilt at `main@b356b2c` (recipe stamp `cb0f758e2975…`)
- Model / Served name / settings: n/a — bring-up fails during image shipping, before the serve starts
- How you started the serve: `./start.sh` (stamp-mismatch auto rebuild)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `git pull` to `b356b2c` on the head, run `./start.sh`.
2. The recipe stamp mismatches, the head rebuilds the image (build succeeds), then `ship_image_to_worker()` runs and the whole pipeline dies:

```
[glm53-exl3] image recipe 536c0af9b302 != repo cb0f758e2975 — rebuilding (SKIP_BUILD=1 keeps GHCR)
[glm53-exl3] building ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3-instanttensor from Dockerfile stamp=cb0f758e2975 (log: /home/vp309/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/logs/build-sm121.log) ...
[glm53-exl3] shipping ghcr.io/miaai-lab/glm-5.3-flash-2x-dgx-sparks:exl3-instanttensor (linux/arm64) to worker via docker save | ssh docker load ...
max depth exceeded
[glm53-exl3] docker save --platform linux/arm64 failed — retrying without --platform
max depth exceeded
```

**Expected results:** the worker loads the image and bring-up continues.

**Actual results:** the worker-side `docker load` fails with `max depth exceeded` on both attempts. The error is the worker daemon's stderr relayed back through ssh — `ship_image_to_worker()` misattributes it to `docker save` (see the "docker save --platform failed" warning above; see Diagnosis below).

## Diagnosis

- `docker save --platform linux/arm64 <IMAGE> -o /tmp/glm53.tar` on the head: **exit=0** — the save side is fine; the failing command is `docker load` on the worker.
- `docker inspect -f '{{len .RootFS.Layers}}' <IMAGE>` → **126 layers**.
- overlay2's *runnable* budget is not the often-quoted 127 but **~125 layers in practice**: every layer adds a `lowerdir=` path to one PAGE_SIZE-limited mount-option string ([moby/moby#46740](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/46740); Tanzu's docs phrase it as "when an image's layer depth exceeds 125 … 'max depth exceeded'"). 126 > 125 → the worker cannot register/mount the chain, while the **build path on the head tolerates the same depth** — the exact asymmetry `582fac8`'s CHANGELOG already documented for the 128-layer case: *"Docker overlay2 could build but could not instantiate on the target hosts"*.
- Layer regression since `582fac8` (−5 layers, with almost no headroom left):
  - `41d1da4` (#289, Sep 28) added **2** separate layers: a `COPY` + a `RUN` for `patch_dflash2_exl3.py`;
  - `b356b2c` (#203, Sep 30) added **3** more: two `COPY`s + one `RUN` for `patch_indexer_warmup_range.py` / `test_indexer_warmup_range.py`.
  - Net: the recipe is back over the budget, and every stamp-mismatch rebuild now produces an unloadable image on the second node.

Note for anyone hitting this today: `SKIP_BUILD=1` does **not** recover the cluster by itself — the rebuild already overwrote the last-good tag, so the local image is the 126-layer one. Workarounds until this is fixed: squash the built image before shipping (`pip install docker-squash`; it preserves the config/labels, including `glm53.recipe.stamp`, so the launcher will not try to rebuild again), or apply the layer merge from the linked PR and rebuild once with `BUILD=1`.

## Proposed fix

1. **PR (linked below):** merge the five #289/#203 steps back into single layers exactly the way `582fac8` did for kpool (−5 layers → 121), keeping the wiring-test coverage pointed at the merged lines.
2. Follow-ups worth considering separately:
   - after `build_image()`, assert `docker inspect -f '{{len .RootFS.Layers}}' "$IMAGE"` stays ≤ ~120 and die with a clear message — the current failure mode surfaces only on the worker, an hour of head-scratching away from the cause;
   - `ship_image_to_worker()` should distinguish save vs load failures (e.g. tag the relayed stderr `[worker]`), since the "docker save --platform failed" message points at the wrong node;
   - consider `--provenance=false` on the `docker build` line as hygiene — attestation-manifest indexes would break this same `save | load` path on containerd-image-store hosts ([issue #8](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks/issues/8) is the adjacent precedent).

`main@b356b2c` regressed over overlay2's practical runnable layer budget — the same failure mode `582fac8` fixed for #280. `41d1da4` (#289) added two separate layers (a COPY + a RUN for `patch_dflash2_exl3.py`) and `b356b2c` (#203) added three more (two COPYs + one RUN for `patch_indexer_warmup_range.py` and its test), bringing the image to **126 layers**, past the ~125-layer mount budget overlay2 actually enforces: every layer appends a `lowerdir=` path to a single PAGE_SIZE-limited mount-option string ([moby/moby#46740](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/46740)).

## The bug

`GLM53_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT` is declared, guarded and forwarded on `start.sh` (TP=2) only. `start-tp3.sh` never mentions it: no declaration, no enum guard, no `--default-chat-template-kwargs` in either inner script, nothing in `serve_env` or the head's `-e` list.

So a TP3 seat ignores the knob completely. An operator who sets it in the shared `.env` gets a silent no-op — the value reaches neither rank — and every client that sends no `reasoning_effort` falls through to `files/chat_template.jinja`, which resolves an absent effort to `max` rather than the intended `high`.

Measured on a live TP3 seat (one question, four request shapes):

| request | completion tokens |
|---|---:|
| no `chat_template_kwargs` | 775 |
| `reasoning_effort: high` | 401 |
| `enable_thinking: true` | 742 |
| `enable_thinking: true` + `reasoning_effort: high` | 362 |

The per-request knob works; there was simply no server-side default. `GLM53_DEFAULT_REASONING_EFFORT` was absent from the running container's env entirely.

The existing `tests/test_default_reasoning_effort.sh` only exercises `start.sh`, which is why the gap went unnoticed.

## The fix

Mirrors `start.sh` into `start-tp3.sh`, adapted to how TP3 keeps its per-rank env:

- **Declaration** with `start.sh`'s empty-default convention (`${VAR-}`), placed *before* `.env.tp3` is sourced so the TP3 env file still wins. Unset and explicitly empty both mean "leave the template fallback alone" — no existing seat changes behaviour until an operator opts in.
- **Guard** with the same `low|high|max` enum check. `medium` stays refused because the template does not recognise it and would render it as `Max`.
- **`--default-chat-template-kwargs`** in *both* inner scripts (head rank 0 and headless worker), beside `--chat-template` — which is the template it parameterises.
- **Forwarding** to worker ranks 1 and 2 through the shared `serve_env` loop, and to the head through its own `-e` list. The head line keeps its line continuation: without the `\` the docker command would end on that line and the next `-e` would parse as a separate command.

New `tests/test_default_reasoning_effort_tp3.sh` pins all five claims against `start-tp3.sh`'s own text. It **fails on the pre-fix launcher** (exit 1, 18 assertion failures) and passes after.

title: Fix mid-serve JIT spike on big prefills

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Important scoped work; schedule after P0 and P1

body:
## Description and Motivation

`BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel.get_warmup_keys` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`) enumerates
the Triton specialization space it wants warmed with `query_slice_start=WarmupIntRange(0, 2)`.
`WarmupIntRange` is exclusive (`range(start, stop)`), so the warmup only ever covers `{0, 1}` — the
`%16==0` and `==1` buckets. Triton's third int bucket ("neither") was never warmed.

Runtime `query_slice_start` values come from `split_indexer_prefill_chunks`' sub-chunking-on-M offsets
(`max_q = max_logits_elems // chunk_n`). With the default 512 MiB logits budget, `index_kpool=4` and
MNBT=7168, sub-chunking first triggers above ~74,897 uncompressed tokens, and any non-power-of-two
compressed length then yields a `max_q` that is neither 1 nor divisible by 16 (e.g. a ~90k-token agent
context → `max_q=5965`). The first big prefill after a restart then pays a cold Triton load of that
variant mid-serve, which the JIT monitor reports as a latency spike:
`Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: BuildPrefillChunkMetadataKernel.kernel`.

Confirmed from the persistent Triton cache (52 entries for this kernel): the only serving-time-created
variants are exactly the `qs_start=''` ones (4 entries, Aug 29 / Sep 2), while all 24 boot-warmup
variants carry boot mtimes — the gap is precisely this bucket.

**Change:** one content-only line, shipped as a repo-convention overlay patch
(`overlay/patch_indexer_warmup_range.py`, Dockerfile COPY+RUN) plus its test:

```
-            query_slice_start=WarmupIntRange(0, 2),
+            query_slice_start=WarmupIntRange(0, 3),
```

Post-fix warmup covers {0,1,2} × {1,15,16} × {aligned, misaligned} × CR {1,4} = 36 keys, a superset of
every variant observed in the cache (including the never-compiled `qs_start='' × misaligned-pointer`

title: preflight: show which interface owns an empty GID index, and the usual cause

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Important scoped work; schedule after P0 and P1

body:
## Why

The CX7 preflight refuses to start when the configured GID index is empty on any device listed
in `HEAD_CX7_IB` / `WORKER_CX7_IB`. Refusing is right (an all-zero entry kills that rank ~60 s
in with `ibv_modify_qp` errno 61), but the output leaves the operator to work out *why* the
index moved — and the most common cause is not obvious from the tables alone:

NetworkManager's default `ipv6.addr-gen-mode=stable-privacy` puts a **second** IPv6 link-local
on the interface. Each address consumes a v1/v2 GID pair, so the IPv4 entry lands at index 5/6
instead of 2/3. On a dual-rail kit there is then **no single index valid on all listed
devices**, and the start is refused. It shows up after a reboot, because whether the privacy
address exists when the GID table is built depends on address ordering at boot.

Written up in detail, with the fix (`addr-gen-mode eui64` and/or an mlx5 rebind to rebuild the
table), in the companion docs PR.

## What changes

Failure path only — **+11 / −1 lines, no behaviour change when the check passes**:

* when an index is empty, also print which interface owns that device and that interface's
  addresses (head and worker), so the extra `inet6` entry is visible at a glance;
* next to the existing "pick each node's `::ffff:<ip>` entry" hint, name the cause and the two
  fixes.

## Evidence

The patched block was extracted and run standalone on the reporting kit with an **empty** index
(`HEAD_GID=WORKER_GID=7`) and with the real indices (`3/3`):

```
=== A. index 7 (empty) — new diagnostics ===
[warn] head GID index 7 is EMPTY on rocep1s0f0
[warn]   rocep1s0f0 -> enp1s0f0np0: inet=10.0.0.1/24
[warn] head GID index 7 is EMPTY on roceP2p1s0f0
[warn]   roceP2p1s0f0 -> enP2p1s0f0np0: inet=10.0.1.1/24
[warn] worker GID index 7 is EMPTY on rocep1s0f0
[warn]   rocep1s0f0 -> enp1s0f0np0: inet=10.0.0.2/24 inet6=fe80::4ebb:47ff:fe80:ea55/64
[warn] worker GID index 7 is EMPTY on roceP2p1s0f0
[warn]   roceP2p1s0f0 -> enP2p1s0f0np0: inet=10.0.1.2/24
[warn] GID tables — pick each node's ::ffff:<ip> entry whose type is RoCE v2;
[warn] the two indices need not match, and a v1 entry at the same index will not work:
[warn] if an index moved after a reboot, look for a second IPv6 address on that
[warn] interface: NetworkManager's default ipv6.addr-gen-mode=stable-privacy adds one,
[warn] which pushes the IPv4 GID later in the table. Check with:
[warn]   nmcli -g ipv6.addr-gen-mode connection show <con>; ip -o addr show dev <if>
[warn] Fixing it means one link-local only (addr-gen-mode eui64) and/or a driver
[warn] rebind so the GID table is rebuilt from the current addresses.
    head   rocep1s0f0 gid0: …            <- unchanged table dump follows

=== B. real indices 3/3 ===
(no GID output — the check passes silently, exactly as before)
```

* `bash -n start.sh` clean; the committed blob is LF with no BOM.
* No in-repo test asserts on the preflight's GID output (checked `tests/*`), so the added
  warnings cannot break an existing expectation; the `die` message itself is untouched.

## Description and Motivation

Image-containing tool turns on a three-Spark deployment were spending roughly a minute broadcasting ~230 MB to each remote worker over management Wi-Fi, despite NCCL correctly using CX7 RoCE. EngineCore's wait for a worker response produced the shared-memory broadcast warning; processor/prefix cache hits did not eliminate the bulk tensor broadcast.

The existing `HEAD_HOST_IP`, `WORKER_HOST_IP` and `WORKER2_HOST_IP` settings already solve the endpoint selection. This PR documents the missing routed-triangle setup, corrects the launcher comment that incorrectly requires those addresses to live on the Gloo/bootstrap interface, and makes the existing settings discoverable in `.env.tp3.example` and the README. It adds an opt-in live probe retaining 12 synthetic images across tool-result turns, with socket byte counters and correctness checks.

The guide includes three narrowly scoped host routes, NetworkManager persistence without cycling interfaces, source-bound connectivity checks, graceful redeployment, verification and rollback. Runtime defaults and launcher behavior are unchanged; no new knob, vLLM patch or automatic privileged network modification is introduced. TP2 is unaffected.

## Related Issues

No existing issue is claimed fixed. This addresses slow multimodal worker RPC over management networking, not general prefix-cache eviction, compilation or shared-memory capacity problems.

## Testing

Operator-authorized live before/after on 3× GB10, recipe/image `775a58b`, same EXL3 weights and DFlash2 draft, TP3/EP3, 1M context limit, GMU 0.80, MNBT 7168, four sequences, FP8 KV and 2048 image-token budget. Changed only the three advertised addresses and added/persisted three routes. Gloo/bootstrap remained on management; NCCL remained on RoCE.

| Request | Wi-Fi TTFT | CX7 TTFT |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial image prompt | 95.131 s | 37.917 s |
| Tool follow-up 1 | 56.730 s | 2.298 s |
| Tool follow-up 2 | 61.676 s | 7.888 s |

These are single sequential observations, not medians. The image-history hash and prompt counts matched; each request still sent ~230 MB per worker, with post-change sockets on CX7/PMTU 9000. All six tool calls were correct. The warning reproduced before and did not occur after. Remaining follow-up latency includes DFlash replay/prefill; no fixed TTFT is promised. Exact counts and the reproducible protocol are in the guide.

- All six directed source-bound TCP connectivity checks passed.
- Same image contents across ranks; normal startup warmup passed 24/24.
- Health, model/context metadata, three concurrent short generations, automatic tool calling and `tool_choice=none` passed.
- Candidate containers have no restarts/OOM flags; no broadcast warning, ERROR, Traceback, NCCL WARN or OutOfMemory in candidate logs at final check.
- Saved NetworkManager routes verified by readback; host reboot, full 1M-context inference, prolonged soak and concurrent image workloads were not tested.
- `uv run --with pytest --with jinja2 python -m pytest -q tests/test_start_overrides.py tests/test_launcher_rank_parity.py`: 9 passed.
